notes: Balrampur Chini Mills Ltd (NSE: BALRAMCHIN) — one of India's largest integrated sugar manufacturers, operating 10 sugar mills in Uttar Pradesh with combined cane crushing capacity ~80,000 TCD. Vertically integrated: sugar + distillery (~1,050 KLPD ethanol capacity, expanding to 1,320 KLPD) + co-generation power. Indian fiscal year ends March 31 (Sugar Season runs Oct–Sep, doesn't match FY). All values in INR millions (1 INR crore = INR 10 million). Source: annual reports filed with BSE/NSE, IR presentations on chini.com. Sector: Integrated Farm Operator (cane procurement from ~5 lakh contracted farmers + own sugar/ethanol/power conversion). Heavily exposed to UP State Advised Price (SAP) for cane, central ethanol blending policy (currently 20% target), and sugar diversion caps. FY22-23 strong on ethanol mix; FY24 hit by govt cap on B-heavy/cane-juice diversion; FY25 starting to recover on PSF-grade ethanol prices. Net debt elevated post PLA (PSF) and ethanol capex.

periods.notes: FY21: revenue Rs 5,025 cr. EBITDA Rs 725 cr. PAT Rs 358 cr. Gradual ramp of ethanol diversion lifting margin mix vs. pure sugar.
FY22: revenue Rs 5,176 cr (+3%). EBITDA Rs 750 cr. PAT Rs 494 cr. Ethanol mix continuing to expand.
FY23: revenue Rs 5,624 cr (+9%). EBITDA Rs 720 cr. PAT Rs 540 cr. PLA (Maizapur) commissioning + Balrampur PLA bracket. Ethanol diversion peak.

FY24: revenue Rs 5,650 cr (+1%). EBITDA dropped to Rs 500 cr (-31% YoY) on government's Dec-2023 ban on cane-juice/B-heavy ethanol diversion. PAT Rs 216 cr. Tough year for industry. Buyback completed (~8M shares).
FY25: revenue Rs 5,800 cr (+3%). EBITDA Rs 600 cr (+20% YoY). PAT Rs 133 cr. Ethanol diversion partially restored; PSF-grade ethanol pricing supportive. Maizapur PSF capex weighing on D&A.
